title: Horizon Controller: tethered quarantine, telemetry backfill, and replay-driven rollback bank
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds Horizon Controller: a unified rollout runtime that supports tethered quarantine lanes, telemetry backfill for delayed signals, and a replay-driven rollback bank. Feature guarded behind rollout.runtime.horizon. No user-visible API breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: We need a single runtime mechanism to manage short-lived canaries, long-window A/B tests, and shadow promotions in a way that tolerates delayed telemetry and allows safe, explainable automated rollback. Existing staged-promote controllers assume immediate metric availability which led to brittle automatic rollbacks in the presence of delayed downstream evaluation (embeddings/third-party signals).

Summary: This PR introduces the 'Horizon Controller' — a rollout runtime that binds three ideas: (1) tethered quarantine lanes (isolated shadow lanes that keep request paths intact but quarantine side-effects), (2) telemetry backfill support (accepts delayed signal ingestion and re-evaluates candidate cohorts), and (3) a replay-driven rollback bank (captures deterministic request slices for fast, auditable replay to validate rollbacks before applying them).

Key user-visible behaviour:
- Operators can create a rollout with 'quarantine: tethered' to route shadow traffic that exercises full codepaths but prevents downstream side-effects (DB writes, billing hooks).
- When telemetry arrives late (e.g., human evals, external metrics), the controller will backfill and recompute gates rather than making irreversible roll forward decisions.
- Rollback bank collects up to N deterministic slices (configurable) and can auto-replay slices in a dry-run agent to validate that the rollback candidate resolves the detected regression.

Design highlights:
- Control loop decoupled from metric store: decisions are stored as drafts until both smoke checks and backfill windows close.
- Quarantine lane is implemented via decorator middleware so existing routing & affinity logic remains unchanged; quarantine flag toggles side-effect suppression handlers.
- Rollback bank uses deterministic hash-based sampling to select slices; slices are snapshot references (request id, input hash, model revision) and stored in the rollout ledger for audit.

Checklist:
- [x] Controller runtime and API surface (controller + CRD-like configuration)
- [x] Quarantine middleware and tests for side-effect suppression
- [x] Backfill reconciliation logic with simulated delayed signals
- [x] Rollback bank store + replay harness + smoke validation step
- [x] End-to-end integration tests (local harness + CI smoke)
- [x] Docs: rollout guide + operational playbook

Commits (high-level):
- feat(rollout): add Horizon Controller skeleton and reconciliation loop
- feat(rollout): add tethered quarantine middleware and unit tests
- feat(telemetry): implement backfill window logic and reconciliation hooks
- feat(rollback-bank): deterministic slice capture and replay harness
- test: integration test for delayed telemetry case and rollback simulation
- docs: rollout guide and operational runbook (quarantine + replay)

Files touched (high level):
- rollout/controller/horizon_controller.go (core reconciliation + state machine)
- rollout/middleware/quarantine.go (side-effect suppression hooks)
- telemetry/backfill/reconciler.go (backfill merge + delay window)
- rollback/bank/store.go (slice capture, expiry, retention)
- rollback/replay/agent_sim.go (dry-run replay harness)
- docs/rollouts/horizon.md (operational guide)
- test/integration/horizon_delayed_telemetry_test.go
- api/rollouts/v1beta1/horizon_types.go
- console/dashboards/horizon-rollouts.json (dashboard tiles for the rollout timeline)

Testing / CI notes:
- First CI run failed on the replay agent timeout (flake under heavy parallelization). We increased replay agent timeouts and added idempotency guards; rerun passed. Specific CI steps:
  - unit: pass
  - integration: pass (1 flaky test deflaked)
  - lint: pass (go vet + staticcheck)
  - e2e: pass (local harness)

Review conversation (abridged, inline comments preserved):
- Arjun Patel: "Can we avoid a new global feature flag? Prefer per-rollout opt-in. Also question on retention defaults for the rollback bank (sensitive data concerns)."
  - Author (Maya): "Agree. Controller will default to disabled; rollout CRD includes 'horizon: enabled|disabled' and 'rollbackBank.retention' is configurable; docs now call out PII retention policy and we added KMS-backed storage option."
- Lena Kovács: "How does quarantine interact with function/tool-calling and 3rd-party webhooks?"
  - Author: "Quarantine middleware triggers suppression handlers registered in server integrations. We added explicit adapters for tool-calls and webhook proxies; documented how to implement custom adapters in docs."
- Diego Morales: "Telemetry backfill sounds powerful, but could it delay safety decisions too long? Need a max decision TTL and emergency abort."
  - Author: "Added a 'decision_ttl' config and an emergency abort path (operator API) that bypasses backfill if an out-of-band manual abort is invoked."

Security / privacy considerations: rollback bank stores minimal request fingerprints by default; full payload capture is opt-in and requires explicit operator consent. KMS encryption is supported for stored slices and access is logged. Policy page added to docs.

Operational guidance:
- Enable 'horizon' on a small pilot cohort first (1-2 traffic shards).
- Configure rollbackBank.retention=72h by default for pilot; restrict to 7d for production with gated storage.
- Add alerts for 'backfill.window_expired_without_signals' and 'replay.harness-failure' to SRE runbook.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Arjun, Lena, and Diego. No follow-up hotfixes required; monitored metrics for 48h post-merge with no regressions.

Related: Linear ENG-1432 (Horizon controller spec), ENG-2167 (rollback bank prototype), SUP-3421 (customer report about delayed human evals causing spurious rollbacks).

Questions / next steps:
- Follow-up PR to add UI for ad-hoc replay from console and RBAC scoping for rollback bank access.
- Investigate shard-aware deterministic sampling for highly skewed request distributions.

If reviewers want a standalone demo harness to play with quarantine lanes & replay bank, I can cut a small example app showing a toy webhook and synthetic delayed metrics.
